description:
RFC 8621 §5.1 (rfc8621.txt:3849-3906) defines SearchSnippet/get arguments as
exactly:
- accountId
- filter
- emailIds  ← only this, no threadIds

The `threadIds: "Id[]"` field at rfc8621.txt:4474 is in §7.3 (EmailSubmission/
query FilterCondition), NOT in §5.1 SearchSnippet/get.

Current code (src/methods/search_snippet.rs:30-55) takes `thread_ids:
Option<&[Id]>` and emits `threadIds` on the wire when provided. Comments in
tests/search_snippet_smoke_tests.rs:4, 10-11, 134 claim "RFC 8621 §6 allows
both" — wrong on two counts: (a) SearchSnippet is §5 not §6, and (b) the
spec does not allow threadIds at all.

Impact: a strict server returns `invalidArguments` per RFC 8620 §3.6.3. A
lenient server (Stalwart, Cyrus) likely accepts it as a vendor extension.
The client API silently exposes a non-portable extension as if it were
spec, leading consumers to build feature-flag dependencies on a non-spec
shape.

Fix options:
  (a) Drop the `thread_ids` parameter entirely. Cleanest. Forces callers to
      resolve threads → emails via Thread/get first.
  (b) Keep `thread_ids` but document it as a non-spec extension. Pros:
      pragmatic. Cons: locks in a non-spec API and consumers will assume
      portability.
  (c) Move it to a separate `search_snippet_get_extension_*` shape (or
      behind a feature flag) so it is impossible to use accidentally.

Recommend (a) for the canonical-template kit, since the kit is supposed to
be spec-conformant and downstreams that need the vendor extension can
build it themselves.

While fixing, also correct the §6 → §5 doc citations in
search_snippet_smoke_tests.rs and the "RFC 8621 §5" comments in
search_snippet.rs.
title: search_snippet_get: thread_ids param is non-spec — RFC 8621 §5.1 defines only emailIds
